subject: Energy
title: Nuclear Energy's Role in Climate
description: A micro-lesson that makes Nuclear Energy's Role in Climate usable.

hook.text: Nuclear power produces virtually zero carbon during operation—making it one of the lowest-emission electricity sources.

buildup.text: Over its full lifecycle (mining, construction, operation), nuclear emits about 12 g CO₂/kWh—comparable to wind.

discovery.text: Nuclear provides about 10% of world electricity—without it, global emissions would be significantly higher.

twist.text: Many climate models show it's extremely difficult to reach net zero without expanding nuclear alongside renewables.

climax.text: Countries like France derive 70% of electricity from nuclear—and enjoy some of Europe's lowest carbon grids.

punchline.text: Splitting atoms to save the climate—nuclear's paradox.

quiz.question: How do nuclear lifecycle emissions compare to wind?
